title: Error Handling Quiz
description: Practice try/except, reading tracebacks, raising errors, and common exceptions.

questions.prompt: Which block catches exceptions in Python?
questions.explanation: try runs code; except handles specified exception types.

questions.prompt: What does except ValueError: do?
questions.explanation: Naming an exception type limits what the except block handles.

questions.prompt: What is a traceback?
options: A report showing where an error occurred and the call chain
questions.explanation: Tracebacks list file, line, and function calls leading to the exception.

questions.prompt: You can read the bottom line of a traceback to see the exception type and message.
questions.explanation: The last line usually states something like ValueError: invalid literal.

questions.prompt: What does raise ValueError("bad input") do?
options: Creates and throws a ValueError with that message
questions.explanation: raise stops normal flow and propagates an exception to callers or except blocks.

questions.prompt: Which exception is raised by int("abc")?
questions.explanation: Invalid conversion to int raises ValueError.

questions.prompt: What happens if an exception is not caught?
options: The program terminates and prints a traceback
questions.explanation: Uncaught exceptions bubble up and stop execution with a traceback.

questions.prompt: What does d["missing"] raise when the key is absent?
questions.explanation: Dictionary lookup with [] on a missing key raises KeyError.

questions.prompt: A bare except: catches all exceptions including KeyboardInterrupt.
questions.explanation: Bare except is broad; prefer specific types and avoid masking system exits.

questions.prompt: What does the else clause on a try block run?
options: When no exception occurred in try
questions.explanation: try/except/else: else runs if try completed without raising.

questions.prompt: What does finally do?
options: Runs whether or not an exception occurred
questions.explanation: finally is for cleanup code that must run in all cases.

questions.prompt: Which is raised when dividing by zero?
questions.explanation: Division or modulo by zero raises ZeroDivisionError.

questions.prompt: What does except Exception as e: give you?
options: A reference to the exception instance in e
Only the error message as a string in e always
questions.explanation: as e binds the caught exception object for logging or inspection.

questions.prompt: SyntaxError happens before the program runs, often when parsing invalid code.
questions.explanation: Syntax errors are detected at compile/parse time, not during normal runtime logic.

questions.prompt: What is IndexError?
questions.explanation: Accessing list[i] with an invalid index raises IndexError.

questions.prompt: Why handle expected errors with try/except?
options: Provide friendly recovery instead of crashing
questions.explanation: Handle predictable failures (bad input, missing files) with clear user-facing behavior.

questions.prompt: What does TypeError usually mean?
options: An operation was applied to the wrong type
questions.explanation: TypeError: unsupported operand or wrong argument types.

questions.prompt: After except handles an error, execution continues:
options: After the try/except block unless you re-raise
At the line that caused the error
questions.explanation: Unless you raise again or exit, code after the block runs normally.

questions.prompt: It is good practice to catch only the exceptions you expect and can handle.
questions.explanation: Specific except clauses avoid hiding unexpected bugs.

questions.prompt: What does FileNotFoundError indicate?
options: An open() or similar call could not find the file
A list index was too large
questions.explanation: FileNotFoundError is a common OSError subclass for missing paths.
